extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for the Journal of Fluid Mechanics (JFM)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting manuscripts to the Journal of Fluid Mechanics, including article-type-specific rules, formatting, ethical and disclosure requirements, and file/media preparation. Targeted at researchers/authors in fluid mechanics who intend to submit to JFM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and originality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To be within the scope of JFM, a paper must present fully developed and supported primary original research with significant fluid mechanical insight, substantially advancing understanding. Every JFM paper is expected to have a clear conclusion that spells out the significant contributions made to the advancement of fluid-mechanical understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure about suitability contact the Editorial Office. Authors must submit a statement explaining how the manuscript contains 'fully developed and supported original research with significant fluid mechanical insight, substantially advancing understanding' (statement helps Editor/Reviewers assess scope; will not be published).

rubrics_metrics.name: Article types and their expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: JFM accepts several article types (JFM Papers/Standard articles, JFM Rapids, JFM Perspectives, Focus on Fluids, Corrigendum, Editorials), each with specific aims and constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JFM Papers: comprehensive original research with no strict length but must address open fluid-mechanics question. JFM Rapids: short (10 page limit), timely, high-impact results; referees asked to comment on timeliness, potential exceptional impact, and clarity/completeness of arguments; Rapids are not preliminary reports nor brief extensions of prior work. JFM Perspectives: invited critical surveys (~50–70 pages) for non-specialists entering a field. Focus on Fluids: invited ~4 page highlights of recent JFM article.

rubrics_metrics.name: JFM Rapids page/length constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Rapids manuscripts are restricted in length on submission to be at most 10 pages when compiled with an unmodified JFM LaTeX style file including all appendices, figures, and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapids review is faster (typical submission-to-publication under 100 days, first decision within 30 days). Authors must highlight timeliness and potential exceptional impact. Supplementary material cannot be used to shorten the manuscript artificially; doing so may lead to transfer to Standard track or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers should feature a single-paragraph abstract of no more than 250 words, which provides a summary of the main aims and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should not spill onto the second page of the manuscript (when constructed with LaTeX using the JFM style). See JFM guide to writing an effective abstract for further help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphical abstract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A graphical abstract is required in addition to figures in the main article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The image will be used as a small thumbnail; multiple panels are not suitable and will be rejected. Image must be aspect ratio 1.2:1 (e.g. 6cm x 5cm landscape), submitted in GIF or high-resolution JPEG (300 dpi). Vector graphics preferred. Text is actively discouraged; if used it must be legible at thumbnail size (2.4cm x 2cm). Captions are not required. Graphical abstracts will be considered for JFM cover selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords and MSC codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may choose up to 3 keywords from the list of JFM Keywords to help select referees; MSC Codes are optional and should be added under the Abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not enter keywords in the manuscript; choose them during online submission and they will be added during typesetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main document format and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to compose papers in LaTeX using the jfm.cls style file; LaTeX is mandatory for JFM Rapids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a PDF generated from LaTeX via the submission site. For review the PDF should be no more than 6MB. There is no need to submit source files with initial submission, but upon acceptance LaTeX source, individual figure files and a final PDF must be submitted for typesetting. Word is allowed for standard papers but will increase production time; equations must NOT be converted to picture format and file must be saved with 'make equation editable' option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical notation and journal style
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should write clearly and concisely in English, adhering to JFM's established style for mathematical notation (see JFM Template). Metric units should be used throughout and all abbreviations must be defined at first use. British spelling must be used (Shorter Oxford English Dictionary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define all variables/entities upon first use. Footnotes are not normally accepted. Glossaries or lists/tables of abbreviations are not permitted. Take care to follow recent JFM pages for style examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures: formats and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred figure format is vector PDF or EPS (with editable labels and colour in RGB). Bitmap/raster formats at a minimum of 300 dpi (EPS, PNG, TIFF) acceptable for photos/imaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal will publish bitmap/raster figures at 150 dpi (and higher option 300 dpi). Minimum acceptable line width is 0.5pt. Each figure must have a single caption beneath it, be cited in the text, appear in the order first mentioned, and files named accordingly (e.g. 'Fig1.eps'). All figure labels will be relabelled by the typesetter—check carefully at proof stage. Failure to follow figure guidelines may cause resupply requests and production delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: numbering and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables, however small, must be numbered sequentially in the order they are mentioned in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lowercase words 'table 1, table 2' throughout. Provide captions and ensure they are cited in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure/table/movie labelling conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative materials should be referred to in text as 'Figures' and words 'figure 1, table 1 and movie 1' should be lower case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number consecutively in Arabic numerals. Figure files must be named to assist production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Movies / video files
rubrics_metrics.description: Movies will be considered integral to the paper and will be part of what is refereed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Movie files should be MP4 (H.264), designated 'Movie'. Each movie must be accompanied by explanatory captions, be referred to in the paper, numbered in order mentioned and titled movie 1, movie 2 etc with separate captions. Maths terms in movies should be bounded by $$ and written in TeX. Each movie should be no more than 50MB. Upon publication movies are hosted online alongside the final article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Material not essential to understanding/supporting a manuscript may be submitted as supplementary materials and will be published online alongside the article but not in the printed pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types include appendices, additional tables/figures, datasets, videos, sound files. Supplementary materials are formal academic record and cannot be retracted/modified other than via article correction processes. They will not be typeset or copyedited—supply them exactly as intended to appear online. Supplementary material must be completely ancillary; it cannot be used to shorten the main paper artificially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Purely technical material may be included in appendices to avoid disrupting narrative flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices should corroborate or add to the main result, be essential for understanding, be a small proportion of the paper, and must not be longer than the paper itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: JFM Notebooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can provide interactive JFM Notebooks (Jupyter) hosted via CoCalc to link underlying data and code associated with article figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notebooks allow readers to interrogate data and code. Detailed instructions for preparing/submitting JFM Notebooks are on the dedicated page; contact jfmeditorial@cambridge.org with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for copyrighted material
rubrics_metrics.description: If the article contains material the author does not own copyright to (figures, charts, tables, photographs, text excerpts), permission from the copyright holder must be obtained to reuse the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are responsible for obtaining permissions and paying any fees; a copy of each permission statement must be sent at acceptance. Follow guidance on seeking permission to reuse figures from Cambridge products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations and references format
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers in References must be cited in the article and vice versa. Use citation styles illustrated in the JFM Template (e.g. 'It has been shown (Rogallo 1981)' using \citep, 'recent work by Dennis (1985)...' using \citet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: natbib package may be used. References can be built from individual \bibitem commands or BibTeX. Where up to ten authors, list all names; where more than ten, list first name followed by et al. JFM discourages citations of manuscripts posted only on social media or pre-print servers that have not been peer-reviewed or published in journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and mandatory end-of-manuscript sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, all articles must include the following sections added at the end of the manuscript before References: Acknowledgements, Funding statement, Competing Interests (compulsory), Data availability statement, Author contributions, Ethical guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More information and specific policies are provided in the linked sections. Examples are given for Funding statements and Competing Interests wording. Competing Interests declarations will be subject to editorial review and may be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding statement guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of sources of financial support for all authors, including grant numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format provided; multiple grant numbers separated by commas and multiple agencies separated by semi-colon with 'and' before final funder. Identify grants belonging to different authors by initials. If no specific funding, use the statement: 'This research received no specific grant from any funding agency, commercial or not-for-profit sectors.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must include a competing interest declaration in the main manuscript file; the submitting author must include declarations relevant to all contributing authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing interests include financial, professional, contractual or personal relationships. Example wording provided. If none exist, state 'Competing interests: The author(s) declare none'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are highly recommended to provide a Data Availability Statement describing how readers can access resources necessary to replicate findings, or explain embargoes/legal/ethical/commercial restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See JFM's Research transparency policy and additional guidance on making resources accessible. Statements promote transparency and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship agreement and contributor roles (CRediT)
rubrics_metrics.description: All listed authors must agree that those listed meet disciplinary norms for authorship and no legitimate author has been excluded. On submission corresponding author is prompted to provide contributor details using the CRediT taxonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRediT includes 14 roles to describe contributions. All parties who contributed but do not meet authorship criteria should be recognised in terms of CRediT. Corresponding author is expected to have authority to act on behalf of co-authors and must confirm this at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Author affiliations should represent the institution(s) at which the research was conducted/supported/approved. For non-research content, affiliations should represent current author institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See author affiliation policy and FAQs for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID requirement for corresponding author
rubrics_metrics.description: All corresponding authors are required to identify themselves using ORCID when submitting a manuscript to this journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't have an ORCID iD you will need to create one; ORCID can be linked in ScholarOne or supplied during submission. ORCID improves discoverability, convenience, and record-keeping. Use the 'Published Name' field to communicate preferred name/pronouns; name-change policy covers formal name changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and declaration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT) should not be listed as authors. Use of AI tools must be declared and described where they were used to generate text/images or to analyse/extract insights from data/materials. Minimal non-generative uses (spelling checks, single words/phrases, minor formatting) do not require declaration, but authors remain accountable for tool use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure whether a use requires declaration, contact the editorial office. Declarations should appear where other assistance is declared: e.g. as acknowledgements/footnote for language editing, in Methods for data analysis, and in figure captions for AI-generated/modified visual content. Declarations should include: name and version of tool, date(s) used, how tool can be accessed by others, full description of how the tool was used, appropriate citations to any third-party text/datasets included in the tool's output. Additionally include proprietary info, modifications to the tool (e.g. training), and any competing interests or potential biases resulting from tool ownership/development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on prior publication / preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted manuscripts should not be under consideration, accepted, or in press at another journal/book unless explicit permission/agreement has been sought from all entities involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposition of a preprint on the author’s personal website, institutional repository, or preprint archive is not viewed as prior or duplicate publication. Follow Cambridge University Press Preprint Policy regarding preprint archives and maintaining the version of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statements for human/animal research
rubrics_metrics.description: Where research involves human and/or animal experimentation, specific statements asserting compliance with national/institutional ethical standards and declarations (e.g. Helsinki Declaration) should be included, with approval committee and approval number as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other specific ethical clearance with details of granting institution should be given in the Methods section. See Cambridge ethical standards and JFM Publishing Ethics page for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: English language editing services (optional guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors (particularly non-native English speakers) may have manuscripts checked by a native speaker before submission; this is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cambridge offers manuscript preparation services including language editing at author's expense. Use of these services is voluntary and does not guarantee acceptance nor restrict submission to Cambridge journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles published by Cambridge must meet accessibility standards outlined in WCAG 2.1 Level AA. Authors should consider colour use, contrast, and text clarity when preparing images and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide image descriptions/alt-text for all figures, tables and multimedia; prepare video/audio descriptions where relevant and submit via Accessibility Descriptions Submission Form. Authors encouraged to prepare their own accessibility materials; if not provided, machine-generated materials will be created and made available at proof stage. Authors are responsible for accuracy. Diagrams, graphs, maps, boxes, code snippets must also be labelled and numbered and referred to as 'Figures'. See guide to Preparing Accessible Materials and Journals Artwork Guide for detailed instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofing and typesetter relabelling caution
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures will be relabelled by the typesetter, so authors must ensure figure labels are carefully checked against originals when they receive proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to check figure labels/captions or follow production guidelines may delay publication and require resupply of files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material permanence and non-typesetting
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary materials are published with the same metadata as the parent article and are considered part of the formal academic record; they will not be typeset or copyedited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They cannot be retracted or modified except via article correction processes; supply them exactly as intended to appear online and be familiar with the detailed guidance on supplementary materials prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrigenda policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrigenda will be published that alter significant conclusions made in a paper and will be clearly linked with the original article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Journal does not normally publish Corrigenda to amend typographical errors, so careful checks at every stage (including proofs) are extremely important.
